summary: Electricity dues from previous owners; whether recoverable from subsequent purchasers; regulatory regime analysis (Electricity Acts 1910, 1948, 2003); interpretation of Conditions of Supply; States' rules compared (Kerala, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Assam, West Bengal); arrears as property charge; universal service obligation; legal principles on successor liability; no automatic transfer of dues to transferee; statutory framework examination for electricity connection refusal; standard applied: electricity dues not binding on new owners absent statutory mandate; appeal partially allowed to limit recovery.
legal_provisions_cited: Electricity Act 1910 s.2(c), s.21(2), s.22, s.24
Electricity (Supply) Act 1948 s.5, s.26, s.49, s.70(2)
final_judgment: Appeal partially allowed; transferees not liable for predecessor's full electricity arrears; recovery capped to statutory limits per state regulations; Electricity Boards directed to provide connections upon compliance with modified terms.
